sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Dangerous Goods UN38.3 Drop Testing and CE-RED Electromagnetic Lab

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (national territory, no sub-state fiscal distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties in force
Luxembourg – United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (DTA)
Exchange of information agreements (EOIAs) under Luxembourg double tax treaty network
EU/OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019 implementing the RBE; CSSF Circular 20/744 on AML/CFT requirements; Criminal Code Articles 506-1 et seq.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Luxembourg notary; foreign supporting documents must carry Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte notarié de constitution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original notarial deed deposited with the Luxembourg Business Registers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate of blocked corporate capital (Attestation de blocage de capital)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank certificate, apostilled if from non-recognized EU jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration (Déclaration du bénéficiaire effectif)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled certified copies of passport and proof of address

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn statement of non-bankruptcy (Déclaration de non-faillite)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized or apostilled as per country of issue

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening against PEP lists (EU/UN/domestic), UN/EU autonomous sanctions (incl. OFAC for USD transactions), CSSF AML guidelines, FATF recommendations, and Real Estate/Financial Sector suspicious transaction reporting requirements; continuous monitoring of all UBOs and directors for sanctions and adverse media.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / e-RCS online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate legal form and names are recorded in French; names drawn from Latin alphabet are accepted but must be transliterated into French characters where required; any non-Latin script must be accompanied by an official French translation and apostille where applicable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, same-session refiling with a revised name; formal administrative appeal to the Director of the Luxembourg Business Registers within 30 days; further judicial appeal to the Tribunal de l'Entreprise (Luxembourg commercial court) within 15 days of notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as sole office for a physical testing laboratory; Luxembourg law requires a genuine registered office in Luxembourg where corporate records are kept and administrative management occurs. A virtual office may be used for supplementary correspondence only, never for substantive laboratory operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% for low-risk standard AML profile, but materially higher for an industrial testing laboratory subject to ILNAS/SafetyMet (accreditation) and environmental or occupational-safety unannounced checks.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg civil-law notary fees for drafting and executing articles of incorporation and notarial deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (tariff set by Grand-Ducal regulation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff plus fixed official registrations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official gazette (Mémorial/Resa) publication of incorporation excerpt
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Official Journal of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank certificate of blocked capital / account opening arrangement fee
Apostille and consular legalization of foreign documents (UBO passports, proof of address, background certificates)
Translation and certified French translation of relevant corporate documents
Preliminary AML/KYC and sanctions screening of UBOs and directors (third-party database fees)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for screening packages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial consultation and corporate housekeeping services for SARL formation documentation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 to 710-26 (SARL provisions); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register (Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés et la comptabilité annuelle des entreprises), Articles 9, 16 and 18.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 12, avenue de la Liberté, L-1931 Luxembourg; electronic filing portal: www.lbr.lu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'inscription au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (application for registration in the Trade and Companies Register) filed electronically via the LBR e-formalities module with the certified notarial deed of incorporation annexed, followed by mandatory publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum EUR 12,000 share capital for an SARL, fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation; the funds must be deposited in a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) at a Luxembourg credit institution and released only upon presentation of the RCS registration certificate (Law of 10 August 1915, Article 710-6, amended by the Law of 23 September 2016). A capital between EUR 1 and EUR 12,000 is admissible only if the articles of association restrict distributions until net assets exceed share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company is constituted as a Société à Responsabilité Limitée under the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, with share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [registered address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that [Manager Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant) with full administrative and representation powers, and that the Manager is authorized to file the incorporation registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers, arrange RESA publication, open corporate bank accounts, and complete all ancillary registrations with the AEDT, Chamber of Commerce, VAT and social security authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and approval of articles of association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notaire) and external corporate counsel; company name reservation via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary or counsel to prepare the French-language statuts governing corporate name, registered office, corporate object (battery safety UN 38.3 testing and CE-RED electromagnetic laboratory under ISIC 7120), EUR 12,000 share capital, management structure and duration. Obtain a name reservation certificate from the RCS and confirm the corporate object is not contrary to public policy or the Grand-Duchy's regulated professions rules.
required_dossiers: Identity documents (passport) of all founding shareholders and proposed managers
Draft declaration of ultimate beneficial owners (UBO chart for RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the reserved name is refused or objected to by the RCS, submit an alternate name for reservation and amend the statuts accordingly. If the corporate object is queried as excessively broad or non-compliant, cure by revising the object clause before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of share capital in a blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) or Caisse de Consignation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account (compte bloqué) in the proposed company name, transfer EUR 12,000 by wire (SWIFT), and obtain the bank's blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage). The certificate must state that the funds are frozen until the RCS registration certificate is presented.
required_dossiers: Wire transfer confirmation (payment rail: Wire Transfer / Wise)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC or source-of-funds questions, provide supplementary banking references and source-of-wealth evidence; if the account is refused, transfer the opening to another Luxembourg credit institution or the Caisse de Consignation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) before a Luxembourg notary in the French language. The notary verifies the legal capacity of the subscribers, collects the bank blocked-funds certificate, certifies the final statuts, and delivers certified copies and the archival copy (minute) required for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Original passports of all shareholders and managers
Notary engagement letter and fee proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests corrections, amend the draft through a rectification schedule before signature. If notarization is refused on legality grounds, revise the corporate object clause or liability structure and re-present the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the notarial deed, file the application for registration (demande d'inscription) via the LBR e-formalities portal. Submit the certified notarial deed, the managers' declarations required by Article 34 of the Law of 19 December 2002, the criminal record extracts, and the proof of deposit of share capital. Pay the statutory RCS filing fee (approx. EUR 68.65).
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Manager's declaration of non-conviction under Article 34 of the Law of 19 December 2002
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of each manager
LBR signatures and liability declaration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or demand for regularization, cure within the stated deadline by filing supplementary documents through the notary. Any refusal of registration may be appealed to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 40 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA official electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the LBR automatically transmits the deed and registration particulars for publication in RESA. Legal existence and enforceability of the deed against third parties become effective upon publication.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed annex transmitted by the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, request expedited handling from the LBR helpdesk; any erroneous published particulars are corrected by filing an RCS rectification application with supporting notarial confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chamber of Commerce inscription and DUNS assignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce (Chambre de Commerce) and Statec business register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the mandatory Chamber of Commerce inscription, pay the annual subscription (0.03% of turnover, minimum approx. EUR 195), and obtain the registration certificate and the DUNS number used for invoicing, government filings and EU cross-border recognition.
required_dossiers: Bank account details (IBAN) of the company
List of intended activities (ISIC 7120 / NAICS 541380 codes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Chamber inscription is automatic upon RCS registration; if the subscription invoice or turnover bracket is incorrect, contest in writing within one month at the Chamber of Commerce service desk and provide audited turnover proof.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and social security activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: RCS registration automatically generates the national tax number (matricule) and VAT registration. File AEDT form for VAT activation of the testing services, register as an employer with CCSS if staff are hired, confirm corporate income tax (CIT) and municipal business tax (IRC) standing, and file the initial tax declaration and net wealth tax position.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease and utility proof
Opening balance sheet and capital deposit proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is not auto-issued, submit an AEDT registration request with the RCS certificate and lease; pending CCSS activation, payroll reporting is accepted with a moratorium of 30 calendar days; late tax penalties can be abated by reasoned application to the AEDT director.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Institut Luxembourgeois de la Normalisation, de l'Accréditation, de la Sécurité et qualité des produits et services (ILNAS) and Office Luxembourgeois d'Accréditation et de Surveillance (OLAS)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ISO/IEC 17025 Testing and Calibration Laboratory Accreditation (OLAS) covering UN Manual of Tests and Criteria Section 38.3 (UN 38.3) battery transport safety methods, together with designation as a Conformity Assessment Body under the Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU (RED) and the EMC Directive 2014/30/EU for the CE-RED electromagnetic laboratory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Class 2 classified establishment (établissement classé) subject to mandatory environmental notification and operating authorization under the Law of 9 May 2014 on the prevention and management of environmental risks. A full EIA report is not required for laboratory use of small lithium cells, provided dangerous-goods storage does not exceed the Seveso III Directive 2012/18/EU threshold screening limits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 December 1994 on residual water treatment - pH 6.5-8.5, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L (Directive 91/271/EEC performance values). VOC and particulate emissions from any soldering or cell-opening procedures must respect Directive 1999/13/EC solvent limits and Luxembourg workplace OELs (VLEP) set by ITM. Facility EMC emissions must stay within CISPR 11 Class A limits. Spent lithium cells and battery waste must be managed under the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste and Directive 2006/66/EC, with damaged-cell consignments transported under ADR 2023 packing instruction P903.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for lithium battery storage rooms, requiring EI 60 fire resistance, hydrogen gas detection and Class D fire suppression. Structural load approval for the drop-test rigs and vibration/isolation benches must be issued by the competent building control service. Workplace clearance under the Luxembourg Labour Code covers electrical safety of high-voltage test benches (IEC 61010), emergency evacuation planning, personal protective equipment protocols, and first-aid provisions for thermal battery incidents.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified digital portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu; statutory company registration via Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign founders: (1) execute notarial deed of incorporation and deposit share capital; (2) complete RCS registration to obtain business registration number; (3) apply to AEDT for Luxembourg VAT number on Form 649 once the RCS number is issued; (4) file Form 100/102 with ACD for corporate income tax and obtain the national tax matricule; non-resident entities with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must register through MyGuichet with an authenticated local representative and certified foreign registration extracts
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg law; available elections include VAT grouping (assujetti unique), the corporate income tax fiscal consolidation regime for 95%-owned resident subsidiaries, the IP box election for qualifying intellectual property income (80% exemption), and various ATAD-compliant hybrid mismatch structuring options; Luxembourg does not provide a unilateral pass-through election for SARLs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for small businesses; non-resident suppliers have no threshold for supplies taxable in Luxembourg; EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance sales threshold remains relevant for e-commerce
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate; mandatory structured electronic invoicing (PEPPOL-BII 3.0) for B2G contracts; B2B and B2C e-invoicing is permitted but not mandatory; VAT returns and EC sales lists must be filed electronically; the Luxembourg standard audit file for tax (SAF-T / fichier d'écritures comptables) is required for tax audit purposes for certain taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to: (a) dispatch/transport of goods outside the EU supported by a customs export declaration (SAD) and transport evidence; (b) services closely linked to exported goods and performed directly for the goods; (c) testing and analysis services supplied to a taxable customer established outside the EU where the place of supply is outside Luxembourg, provided the testing relates to goods destined for non-EU delivery or to services effectively enjoyed outside the EU; proof of customer's non-EU status and export destination must be maintained.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Improper or fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger retrospective VAT adjustments over a five-year limitation period (extended to ten years for fraud), a 10% tax increase for late or incomplete reporting, late-payment interest at the legal rate, administrative fines up to EUR 12,500, and criminal penalties of 8 days to 5 years imprisonment; the Luxembourg tax administration may revoke the zero-rating clearance and hold directors personally liable for unpaid VAT in case of repeated infringements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting under the European Central Bank (ECB) framework, together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and financial market supervision and the Ministère des Finances for capital movement statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully integrated eurozone jurisdiction with unrestricted currency convertibility. Both current and capital account transactions are free from exchange controls under EU Capital Movement Directive (Directive 88/361/EEC) and Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, and repatriation of invested capital are freely permitted subject to standard tax withholding obligations, corporate formalities, and CSSF/BCL statistical reporting thresholds; no prior administrative authorization or repatriation permit is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds exists under Luxembourg law. Exporters are freely entitled to retain foreign currency in external/offshore accounts, to convert to EUR at market rates, or to settle liabilities directly in foreign currency. However, under ECB Balance of Payments Statistics Regulation (Regulation EC No 184/2005), direct reporting on cross-border payments and transactions exceeding EUR 12,500 must be furnished to the BCL for statistical compilation. No percentage or timeline for mandatory conversion is imposed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess)
Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for the entity is 'High' for inbound low-value disbursement flows and 'Medium' for statutory capital escrow functions. Luxembourg recognizes European Economic Area (EEA)-licensed E-Money Institutions (EMIs) under Directive 2009/110/EC and Payment Services Directive (PSD2) via passporting. A Luxembourg SARL may open accounts at EEA EMIs such as Wise (European Banking Authority passporting from Belgium, Ireland, or other EU member states). Legal constraints include: (i) EMI accounts cannot hold investment-grade securities; (ii) client money safeguarding obligations may restrict sub-account concentration; (iii) high-value battery testing lab capital injections above EUR 15,000 usually require a licensed credit institution for SWIFT and letters of credit; (iv) EMI onboarding may not satisfy escrow account provisions in third-party capital commitment agreements; (v) KYC and AML requirements under CSSF Circular CSSF 12/552 apply fully to EMIs, requiring enhanced due diligence where shareholders or beneficiaries are not EU tax residents. EMIs are not substitutes for full commercial banking relationships when the entity must issue Commercial Letters of Credit, operate as a non-bank importer/exporter, or rely on an overdraft/credit line.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law and CSSF AML/CTF Circulars (notably CSSF Regulation N° 12-02 and related guidance) mandate that legal entity KYC onboarding require reliable identification of natural persons acting on behalf of the company. Since the entry into force of the Luxembourg electronic identification law (Law of 23 September 2020) and CSSF-sanctioned remote video identification guidelines, a fully remote opening is permissible for directors with valid EU/EEA passports and a qualified electronic signature, provided the remote identification provider is assessed by the CSSF. However, in practice, Tier-1 commercial banks (BNP Paribas, Spuerkeess, Société Générale) routinely require at least one leading director with legal capacity to appear physically at a branch for initial interview and signature verification, especially where the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-EU resident, the shareholder is another corporate entity, or the target account class is 'Capital Escrow Account'. The mandate can be satisfied by the physical appearance of the day-to-day manager or a board member empowered by notarized power of attorney; shipment of certified copies is not accepted for certain high-risk products such as International Trade Services or settlement accounts for the purchase of shares. Physical presence is not mandatory for all directors, but at least one 'A' class signatory must complete a face-to-face or CSSF-approved video interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain comprising non-resident parent entities or ultimate beneficial owners located in jurisdictions with lower regulatory transparency (e.g., non-EU/EEA holding structures).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of beneficial owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), consolidated organizational chart verified by an EU law firm, LEI certificates for each entity in the chain, audited financial statements of the parent entity for the last two years, pass-through documentary evidence of all ownership percentages, and a formal statement by each intermediate UBO consenting to the bank's disclosure regime.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SARL with no established trading history, low issued share capital, and high expected first-year turnover in battery safety laboratory services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Articles of Association (acte constitutif), business plan with revenue forecast and customer pipeline, ISIC 7120 and NAICS 541380 activity descriptor, letters of intent from laboratory users, signed rental contract for premises, laboratory accreditation documents (e.g., UN38.3 testing scope, IEC/ISO 17025 draft), and an opening balance sheet certified by a Luxembourg chartered accountant or auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or day-to-day managers whose residence address is classified as a high-risk jurisdiction or whose identity passes through a proxy/registered-agent service.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport and national ID card, proof of residence not older than three months, independent background check, CV detailing professional experience and laboratory management credentials, confirmation that the proxy/registered-agent arrangement is solely for purpose of physical address and not for beneficial ownership, and a negative sanction-list screening report issued by a reputable external compliance provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to suppliers, calibration providers, or ancillary testing instrument manufacturers involving potential dual-use goods or controlled technology.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Specified commercial invoices and purchase orders matching the battery-testing scope, UN38.3 test procedure documentation, EU Dual-Use Regulation (EU) 2021/821 classification assessment showing no dual-use designation, certifying that all imported equipment is solely for laboratory testing and not for weapons production, export control certificates from the Luxembourg Office of the Ministry of the Economy and from the exporter's authority where applicable, and procurement contract clauses stating end-use and non-re-export obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injections from shareholders domiciled in a third country with high AML/CFT risk, especially where the subscription amount exceeds EUR 50,000.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share subscription agreement, bank references from the sending bank in the shareholder's country, Statement of Source of Wealth (SSW) and Source of Funds (SOF) document, audited financial statements of the shareholder, certified proof of legal existence, confirmations that the shareholder is a licensed operating company rather than a shell entity, and compliance sign-off from an EU-approved agent with access to global sanctions and PEP databases.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection to the SARL's Capital Escrow Account or Operational Account is performed via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder’s bank to the Luxembourg credit institution. Eligible purpose codes must be classified in the BCL's Balance of Payments Manual: for initial equity subscription the transaction falls under 'Direct investment – Equity capital' (BoP code 5101 or equivalent under the ECB BPM6 classification); for shareholder loans, current account advances, or convertible instruments, the codes correspond to 'Loans – Non-Financial Sector' (e.g., BoP code 6101). The remitter must provide the definitive document (share subscription agreement, notarized deed of contribution, or board minutes) and ensure the MWG/MT103 field 70 (Remittance Information) cites the precise invoice/reference number and the phrase 'INCREASE OF SHARE CAPITAL' or 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION' to avoid AML flagging. Verification by the Luxembourg bank will normally require: (i) a certified share subscription deed; (ii) source-of-funds documentation for the remitting account holder; (iii) CSSF/BCL statistical reporting declarations if cumulative cross-border payments exceed EUR 12,500; (iv) a signed confirmation that the SARL has no illegal or unlicensed activity under Luxembourg commercial law; and (v) in case of non-EU remitter, an anti-money-laundering check on the originator's bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for test laboratory equipment, calibration services, and subcontracting is governed by the SARL’s treasury policy. Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for ordinary supplier payments, direct debits, and pre-payments. For high-value or documentary trade transactions, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) can be issued by the Luxembourg account bank in favor of foreign suppliers, payable at sight via a confirming bank in the supplier’s country. The SARL may also use TARGET2 (T2) and SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) for EUR-denominated low-value disbursements to EU beneficiaries. Treasury instructions must specify the ICA (International Code Area) or BT (Bank Transaction) in the instruction, provide the beneficiary bank BIC and IBAN, and maintain a risk-based threshold under which no additional FX conversion is needed. For cross-currency disbursements, the bank will convert EUR to USD/CNY/GBP at spot using the ECB reference rate plus spread; the SARL may request a forward rate when payment exceeds EUR 100,000 and the delivery horizon exceeds 60 days. All outbound transfers must be reported to the CSSF/BCL under the same Balance of Payments statistical reporting-directly mechanism and should be supported by original contracts, invoices, and material import/export certificates to substantiate commercial purpose and avoid sanctions screening failures.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on soft currencies only where underlying cross-border trade settlement requires such hedge, subject to bank counterparty eligibility
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for capital-injection or shareholder-loan multilateral netting
FX swaps for short-term treasury cash flow management between EUR and foreign currencies
Embedded forwards in zero-cost collars or participating forwards when corporate treasury has a confirmed trade receivable/payable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) with management report and auditor's report if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end: shareholder approval within 6 months and deposit with RCS within 1 month after approval; for a calendar-year SARL, by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines up to EUR 2,500; repeated default may trigger adverse publication, director accountability measures, and administrative strike-off after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (déclaration de confirmation de bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of any change in UBO data; if no change, at least once per calendar year, generally before 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and criminal fines up to EUR 1.25 million for entities; persistent non-compliance may lead to judicial dissolution or strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax and municipal business tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) and the local commune for municipal business tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 6 months after the tax year-end; for calendar-year accounts, generally due by 30 June of the following year, subject to ACD extensions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to 10% of the assessed tax, late-payment interest, ex officio assessment, and criminal fines for wilful default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the corporate income tax return; for calendar-year entities, generally due by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties and late-payment interest as for income tax; failure to file permits ex officio tax assessment and may attract administrative fines

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL is exempt from compulsory statutory audit unless it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce of 50 employees; exceeding two of three triggers a mandatory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan comptable normalisé) transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as endorsed by the EU may be applied for consolidated financial statements and is mandatory for listed and certain regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Luxembourg SARL must maintain accurate UBO data with the RBE. Changes in beneficial ownership must be reported within one month; whether or not a change occurs, an annual confirmation of the registered UBO data must be filed at least once per calendar year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,200 - $3,500 for licensed domiciliation services; higher for a dedicated laboratory premises in Luxembourg City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000 - $25,000 for a small SARL in the battery-safety and electromagnetic testing laboratory sector

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% statutory corporate income tax (Impôt sur le Revenu des Collectivités, I.R.C.) plus 7% solidarity surcharge on the I.R.C. and municipal business tax (LCT) of 6.75% in Luxembourg City; combined effective nominal rate ≈ 24.94%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (as from 6% participation or €6M purchase price). Patent Box: 80% exemption of gross IP income (effective rate ≈ 5.2%); Investment tax credit for digitalisation (20%) and environmental assets (up to 12%); R&D super-deduction limited to 13% of eligible R&D spend for qualifying hazardous-goods battery-testing innovation; no de minimis tax regime for SARL derives from the test activity itself.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit; indefinite carryforward under Art. 114 L.I.R.)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 750 – ‘Déclaration de l’impôt sur le revenu des collectivités et des sociétés’ filed via the MyGuichet e-filing portal (myguichet.lu) with authenticated electronic signature; optional paper filing only with prior administrative approval.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months of the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year SARL the return is due by 31 December of the following year (e.g. FY2025 return due 31 December 2026). Extension may be requested by a reasoned application before the deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: legal name, legal form (SARL), registered office, Luxembourg business registration number (matricule), effective management address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a SARL managed from abroad, state the place of central administration in Luxembourg, the local POA, and any permanent establishment details. If no Luxembourg management, the entity may be deemed a resident only if it maintains its registered seat and substance in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year opening and closing dates and accounting currency (EUR required).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate any short or long accounting period and certify that annual accounts are kept in EUR even if revenue is invoiced in foreign currency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit before tax (bénéfice comptable avant impôt), inclusive of all revenue from UN38.3 drop testing, CE-RED electromagnetic compatibility testing, and report issuance fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise revenue under Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP); no deferred revenue is permitted unless a contractual testing milestone is incomplete at the balance-sheet date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible add-backs: corporate income tax, solidarity surcharge, municipal business tax, late-payment interest, fines, penalties, and non-economic gifts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow any tax on profits as a deduction; also add-back excessive management fees paid to a non-resident related party that fail the arm’s-length test under TP rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward offset (déduction des pertes antérieures): enter the amount of prior-year losses being utilised within the year, with a supporting schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL must attach the loss register; losses transferred into Luxembourg from a non-resident parent are never deductible. For losses incurred under a non-resident shareholder change, verify no anti-trafficking denial applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss offset (base imposable). Segment, where applicable, between income sheltered under the participation exemption, patent box exempt portion, and ordinary income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income from foreign testing contracts to the Luxembourg taxable base under the L.I.R. Article 158 rules; no territorial allocation exists – Luxembourg taxes worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculation and credits: I.R.C. at 17% applied to the taxable base above EUR 175,000 (15% on the first EUR 175,000), plus 7% solidarity surcharge, plus municipal business tax (LCT) rate of 6.75%; then subtract any R&D credit, investment tax credit, foreign tax credit, and dividend participation exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the TRC and withholding tax statements if a foreign parent or a foreign PE has paid WHT on dividend/interest income; request a foreign tax credit under the applicable DTA or EU Directives.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due or refund: net I.R.C., solidarity surcharge, LCT, less prepayments and credits; payable to the Administration des contributions directes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities are not entitled to the Luxembourg shareholder relief (RSTA) and must pay the full final corporate tax; the due date is 31 December of the following year (unless a different instalment plan is approved).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% increase on the tax assessed (minimum surcharge applies). Late payment: monthly interest of 0.5% (6% per year). Ex-officio assessment for non-filing adds a 25% increase for gross negligence, and criminal penalties under Art. 396 may apply in case of fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate at source, the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the SARL a current Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign competent authority, together with a signed beneficial-ownership declaration and, where applicable, Form 25/26 for the reduced WHT application, before the dividend is paid. For EU/EEA parent companies holding at least 10% of the SARL for an uninterrupted period of 12 months, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (EU/EEA DTA) reduces withholding tax to 0% upon the same evidence. If the reduced rate is not applied at distribution, a refund claim must be lodged with the Luxembourg Inland Revenue within the time limit of the DTA (usually before the end of the second following year).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and interest paid by a Luxembourg SARL to non-residents are subject to 0% Luxembourg withholding tax (no general WHT on interest or royalties; exceptions apply only to profit-sharing loans or payments effectively connected with a Luxembourg permanent establishment). For deduction purposes, a TRC is still required to substantiate beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory if related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 per transaction category (goods, services, intangibles, financial transactions) in the tax year. Master File mandatory when the group’s consolidated global turnover equals or exceeds EUR 50,000,000. Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) threshold: consolidated group turnover of EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not have a standalone codified ESR similar to the UAE; however, substance is governed by the General Tax Law (AO) and the effective-management test. For a battery-safety testing SARL, economic substance requires: own or leased laboratory premises in Luxembourg, full-time qualified technical staff performing the UN38.3 and CE-RED tests, laboratory insurance, genuine client contracts, and board decisions taken in Luxembourg. A letter-box entity without such substance will be denied treaty benefits under the domestic GAAR (Art. 6 AO / fraude à la loi) and may be reassessed as subject to tax only on a deemed-basis income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Fraude à la loi / Déclaration frauduleuse)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly under-declaring testing fees, issuing duplicate invoices, booking personal expenses as laboratory expenses, or falsifying the UN38.3 test certificates to inflate tax-deductible costs or avoid revenue recognition.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 396 L.I.R.: fine up to EUR 25,000 (or twice the evaded tax), imprisonment from 1 to 5 years (up to 10 years for aggravated evasion), full restitution of evaded taxes, plus late-payment interest at 6% p.a.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SARL’s gérant and the statutory directors are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax underpayment if they signed false declarations, concealed transactions, or actively participated in the fraud. Direct recourse on personal assets, restriction of movement and, in severe cases, custodial sentences for the directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a post-box entity with no employees, no UN38.3 drop-testing equipment, no laboratory premises, and no actual testing activity in Luxembourg; outsourcing all substance to foreign related parties while claiming Luxembourg tax-residence status and treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of Luxembourg tax residency or denial of treaty benefits; recharacterisation of profits under GAAR; disallowance of the full intercompany fee deduction; administrative penalty of 10% of the recalculated tax, plus late interest. In case of non-filing or false substance declarations, criminal prosecution for misuse of rights can follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held civilly liable for all taxes, penalties and interest re-assessed; they may be banned from professional activity and, if complicit, face criminal sanctions for false certification and tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to perform customer due diligence for high-value physical-testing orders (e.g. battery pack qualification fraud), accepting cash payments above statutory thresholds without declaring them, fabricating UN38.3 test reports for foreign clients, or omitting to file a suspicious activity report (STR) when the lab’s invoices are used for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended): administrative fines of up to EUR 1,250,000 or 10% of turnover for serious breaches; criminal money-laundering penalties up to 5 years’ imprisonment and a criminal fine of up to EUR 500,000. The banking AML risk tier for the entity is low-risk, but obligations remain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant, compliance officer, and the statutory directors are personally liable for monetary penalties; they may be arrested and extradited for money-laundering offences, be subject to a professional ban, and be liable for damages suffered by victims or the State.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or submit the Luxembourg Local File, Master File, or CbCR as required, or applying non-arm’s-length fees for intercompany testing services (e.g. charging a parent company EUR 10,000 for a test when the independent market price is EUR 25,000) without providing comparability evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of up to EUR 5,000 for failure to produce TP documentation; transfer pricing adjustment upward with an additional 10% penalty on the corrected taxable income (where the adjustment is for cross-border non-arm’s-length transactions); 6% p.a. late interest; and possible additional cascading penalties for non-disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the additional tax and the 10% penalty if they failed to establish and retain proper TP documentation; in cases of gross negligence, the tax authorities may refer the file for criminal tax-evasion prosecution.
